## Summary

Keating already has a substantial, working voice/audio stack in the `web/` app — including a complete OpenAI Realtime (gpt-realtime) WebRTC implementation with ephemeral tokens, Gemini Live, TTS, and one-shot STT, plus a full voice-mode UI in the chat composer. ## 1. Existing voice/audio infrastructure

### Web app — `web/src/keating/`
- **`speech.ts`** (433 lines) — the orchestration core. Defines `SpeechProvider` interface, provider registry (lazy dynamic imports), settings type `WebSpeechSettings` (persisted to `localStorage` key `keating:web:speech`), the `keating_voice` agent tool (`createSpeechTool`), and Web Audio playback helpers: `getAudioContext()` (with `webkitAudioContext` fallback), `primeSpeechAudio()`, `schedulePcmAudio()` (base64 PCM16 → `AudioBuffer`, 24kHz `RECEIVE_SAMPLE_RATE`), `scheduleAudioBlob()`. Also `speechInputMode()` → `"duplex" | "stt"` and `isDuplexSpeechProvider()` (duplex = `gemini-live`, `openai-realtime`).
- **`speech-providers/openai-realtime.ts`** (373 lines) — **full GPT Realtime / WebRTC implementation**:
  - `mintEphemeralKey()` — POST `https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/client_secrets` with the user's real OpenAI key, returns `client_secret.value` ephemeral token.
  - `RTCPeerConnection` + `createDataChannel("oai-events")` + SDP exchange via POST `https://api.openai.com/v1/realtime/calls` (Content-Type `application/sdp`), using the ephemeral key as Bearer.
  - `attachMicrophone()` via `getUserMedia({audio:true})`, `pc.addTrack`, remote audio played into a hidden `<audio autoplay>` element.
  - Two entry points: `synthesize()` (one-shot TTS-style `response.create`) and `startLiveSession()` (continuous `server_vad` turn detection, `input_audio_transcription: gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`, streaming user/assistant transcript callbacks).
  - Models offered: `gpt-realtime-2` (default), `gpt-realtime`, `gpt-realtime-mini`, `gpt-4o-realtime-preview-2024-12-17`, `gpt-4o-mini-realtime-preview-2024-12-17`. Voices: alloy, ash, ballad, cedar, coral, echo, marin (default), sage, shimmer, verse. Uses `withApiRetry`. Note: talks to `api.openai.com` **directly, not through the proxy**.
- **`speech-providers/gemini-live.ts`** (271 lines) — Gemini Live duplex via `@google/genai` (`GoogleGenAI`, `Modality`), `session.sendRealtimeInput({audio:{data, mimeType:"audio/pcm;rate=16000"}})`, mic capture with `AudioContext({sampleRate:16000})` + `createMediaStreamSource`. Model `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview`.
- **`speech-providers/stt.ts`** (120 lines) — one-shot STT: `startMicRecording()` (`MediaRecorder`), `transcribeAudio()` routing to OpenAI `/v1/audio/transcriptions` (`gpt-4o-transcribe`, via proxy) or Gemini `generateContent` (`@google/genai`).
- **`speech-providers/openai-tts.ts`** (110), **`supertonic.ts`** (101, `@huggingface/transformers` local TTS), **`custom-tts.ts`** (67, user OpenAI-compatible endpoints).

### Web app — UI
- **`components/AssistantChatPanel.tsx`** — voice is a first-class composer mode. `SpeechComposerControl` (mic button, push-to-talk dictation for STT mode) and `LiveVoiceOverlay` (full-screen dialog driving `provider.startLiveSession(...)` with live transcript display and STT fallback). Chooses duplex vs. STT via `speechInputMode()`.
- **`components/SpeechSettingsTab.tsx`** (433 lines) — settings UI (rendered from `components/settings/LearningTab.tsx`) for provider/model/voice/mic toggle/custom endpoints.

### Root CLI — `src/core/speech.ts`
Only voice-tag text scaffolding: `normalizeVoiceUtterance`, `voiceTagLine` (`[voice ...]` markup), `speechStrategySummary`. Config type in `src/core/config.ts` (`speech.enabled/defaultVoice/fastModel/steeringModel`), tool wired in `src/pi/hyper-teacher/tools/speech.ts`. **No actual audio capture/playback in the CLI.** Tests: `test/speech.test.ts`, `web/src/test/openai-speech.test.ts`, `web/src/test/speech-input-mode.test.ts`.

## 2. AI providers, keys, and abstraction

- **Framework: the "pi" framework** — `@earendil-works/pi-ai`, `pi-agent-core`, `pi-web-ui`, `pi-coding-agent`, `pi-tui` (v0.80.2). Model/provider abstraction comes from `@earendil-works/pi-ai/compat` (`getModels`, `getProviders`, `getModel`, `streamSimple`, types `Api`/`Model`/`Context`). The agent is `Agent` from `pi-agent-core` (see `web/src/hooks/useKeatingAgent.tsx`). `@ax-llm/ax` is a root dependency used for prompt optimization (`src/core/ax-optimizer.ts`), not for the chat runtime.
- **Providers configured** (`web/src/lib/provider-models.ts`): `openai`, `anthropic`, `google`, a custom `DIO_PROVIDER_ID` (`web/src/dio-provider.ts`), `browser` (keyless, `@huggingface/transformers`), plus user-defined custom providers (ollama, llama.cpp, vllm, lmstudio, openai-completions/responses, anthropic-messages). Fallback model ids include `gpt-5.5`, `claude-opus-4-8`, `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`.
- **Key management** — via pi-web-ui `getAppStorage()`, NOT Skate. `getProviderApiKey(providerName)` in `web/src/lib/provider-models.ts:353`:
  1. OAuth access token (`getOAuthAccessToken` / `providerToOAuthId`, `web/src/keating/oauth.ts`),
  2. `storage.providerKeys.get(name)` (app storage),
  3. custom provider `apiKey`.
  This same `getProviderApiKey` is threaded everywhere as the `getApiKey` callback: into the agent (`useKeatingAgent.tsx:410,690`), the speech tool (`browser-tools.ts:105`), and `resolveSpeechCredential()`/`startLiveSession()` in the chat panel. `resolveSpeechCredential()` (`speech.ts:152`) prefers a genuine `openai` key, then `google` — deliberately excluding custom-base OpenAI-compatible providers because realtime/transcription endpoints are OpenAI-specific.
- **Proxy** — `web/src/lib/provider-proxy.ts` (`proxiedProviderRequestUrl`, `chatProxyBaseUrl`, `x-target-url` header). Used by STT and TTS; **the realtime provider bypasses it and calls `api.openai.com` directly.**

## 3. Web client architecture — where voice plugs in

- Chat is `@assistant-ui/react` based. `web/src/components/AssistantChatPanel.tsx` is the session/chat view; the composer already hosts `SpeechComposerControl` + `LiveVoiceOverlay`. State is Zustand (`web/src/stores/keating-agent-store.ts`, holds `speechSettings`/`toggleSpeech`). Agent lifecycle in `web/src/hooks/useKeatingAgent.tsx`; streaming in `web/src/hooks/keating-stream.ts`. Routing is `@tanstack/react-router`. **A voice mode UI is already plugged in here — new realtime work would extend `LiveVoiceOverlay` / `openai-realtime.ts` rather than build from scratch.**

## 4. GPT Realtime / ephemeral tokens

Already implemented (see #1). Uses the current Realtime API shape: `POST /v1/realtime/client_secrets` with `{session:{type:"realtime", model, audio:{output:{voice}}}}` for ephemeral minting, and `POST /v1/realtime/calls` for SDP. `session.update` sets `server_vad` turn detection and input transcription. Model list already includes `gpt-realtime`, `gpt-realtime-2`, `gpt-realtime-mini`.

**Root** — AI: `@ax-llm/ax ^22.0.7`, `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`/`pi-tui ^0.80.2`, `@google/generative-ai ^0.24.1`, `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`. No dedicated audio libs.

**web/** — AI: `@earendil-works/pi-agent-core`, `pi-ai`, `pi-web-ui`, `@google/genai ^2.10.0`, `@huggingface/transformers ^4.2.0` (local TTS/STT), `@assistant-ui/react`. **No livekit, deepgram, elevenlabs, or dedicated WebRTC/audio packages** — realtime uses the browser's native `RTCPeerConnection`/`getUserMedia`/`AudioContext`/`MediaRecorder`. `three`/`@react-three/fiber` present for visuals, not audio.

- Exists: OpenAI Realtime WebRTC + ephemeral tokens, Gemini Live, OpenAI/custom/Supertonic TTS, one-shot STT, full voice composer + live overlay UI, settings tab, provider/key resolution, tests.
- Doesn't exist: any realtime/audio in the root CLI (text-only voice tags); LiveKit/Deepgram/ElevenLabs; a server-side ephemeral-token broker (the browser mints ephemeral keys directly with the user's OpenAI key, bypassing the proxy); Opus-specific handling (WebRTC negotiates codecs implicitly).</result>

- `keating tui` (`src/tui/opentui-host.ts`) is a thin RPC client over `launchRpcClient` (`src/runtime/pi.ts`), which spawns pi-coding-agent in RPC mode. All work uses **bun** (see `justfile`). Phases are ordered by dependency: shared provider/secrets groundwork first (needed by the e2e harness and by the TUI verification), then TUI, web search, voice, and finally the e2e harness that exercises everything.

Verified architectural facts this plan relies on:

- `keating tui` (`src/tui/opentui-host.ts`) is a thin RPC client over `launchRpcClient` (`src/runtime/pi.ts`), which spawns pi-coding-agent in RPC mode. The RPC protocol (`node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/modes/rpc/rpc-types.d.ts`) supports `extension_ui_request` methods: `select`, `confirm`, `input`, `editor`, `notify`, `setStatus`, `setWidget`, `setTitle`, `set_editor_text`, answered by `extension_ui_response` with `{value}` / `{confirmed}` / `{cancelled:true}`. **There is no `custom` component over RPC** — `rpc-mode.js` implements `async custom() { return undefined; }` while `hasUI()` is still true.
- **Latent bug**: `quiz` (`src/pi/hyper-teacher/tools/teaching.ts:98`) and `ask_user_question` gate on `typeof ctx.ui.custom === "function" && ctx.hasUI` — both true in RPC mode — then do `await ctx.ui.custom(...)` which resolves `undefined`, so `rawAnswers[q.id]` throws. The TUI path is currently broken for quizzes regardless of the host.
- `RpcClient` (rpc-client.d.ts) exposes `onEvent`, `prompt`, `followUp`, `waitForIdle`, `promptAndWait`, `getMessages`, but no public UI-response method — the host already reaches into `client.send()` via a cast (opentui-host.ts:137-140). Keep that pattern.
- Custom pi providers are registered by writing `models.json` into `configDir(cwd)` — see `syncZyphraProvider` in `src/runtime/pi.ts:108`. This is the mechanism to add MiniMax.
- `skate` CLI is installed (`~/.nix-profile/bin/skate`, v1.0.1).

---

Everything downstream (TUI e2e, CLI web-search testing) needs a working provider with the key from `skate get minimax@secrets`.

## Phase 1 — TUI: generative UI + interactive extension requests in `keating tui`

### 1b. OpenTUI host: service UI requests interactively

  - `goals` tools → goal cards
  - anything else → plain text of the tool result content.
  - If `details` does **not** survive RPC, fall back to parsing the tool result `content` text (the tools already emit `[artifact://…]` markers and paths) — keep the mapping tolerant.
